info.title: Kontor control plane
info.description: The loopback HTTP and SSE contract of one Kontor realm.

post.description:
The kind, the target and the desired state are checked against the domain's own
compatibility matrix before anything is written, and the revision is checked
against what the aggregate currently stands at — so a caller working from a
stale read is told the current revision and nothing is mutated. The write
itself is `kontor-store`'s single transaction: intent, target row, outbox
entry, first durable transition, desired state and the intent event, or none of
them.

409.description: Stale revision or a reused idempotency key

get.summary: The durable control-plane feed.
get.description:
Three properties make it restartable. Every frame's SSE `id` is the event's
own persisted control-plane cursor, so `Last-Event-ID` is a position this
Realm actually allocated. Delivery is strictly greater than the requested
position, so nothing is repeated and nothing is skipped. And the events come
from SQLite rather than from memory, so a reconnect after a restart reads the
same log the previous connection was reading.

200.description: An SSE stream of control-plane events

410.description: The position is outside the retained history

get.summary: Liveness, Realm identity and the startup barrier.
Every project in this Realm.
One project.
Every coding-account profile in one project.
get.description:
Admin, not observer. The tier model puts credential and account routes with
the admin secret, and an account profile names the alias a resolver looks a
credential up under — so even though the alias is not itself a capability,
enumerating them is an account-authority read.

get.summary: One coding-account profile.
One stored work-profile revision, addressed by its open key and version.
get.description:
The key is whatever the deployment called it. Nothing in this route — or in
the CLI and MCP surfaces above it — enumerates the legal values, because a
seeded profile pack is deployment data and a control plane that hard-coded its
names would refuse every profile a deployment added.

get.summary: One command receipt, with its transition history.
Every agent run in one project, optionally one mission's.
Explain what a scheduling pass over one project would decide.
get.description:
Nothing is admitted, queued, launched or leased. This is `kontor_scheduler::plan`
run over a snapshot assembled from stored rows, reported with every blocker.

get.summary: Every task in one project, oldest first.
One task, its active workflow, its gate states and its pinned revisions.
One task's gate states and the evidence they were reduced from.
get.description:
A task with no active workflow answers with an empty inspection rather than a
refusal: the task exists, and "this task has no workflow yet" is a fact about
it rather than a missing row.

get.summary: Every mission in one project.
One mission.
Every external-ticket link in one project.

One ticket's stored evidence: the projection, the last observation, the
conflicts.
One ticket's inbound comments, newest first.
get.description:
Inbound only, and structurally so: there is no outbound comment table in this
schema and no route that writes one.

get.summary: One ticket's convergence attempts, newest first.
This Realm's immutable identity.
One agent run, its projection, its pinned revisions and its recorded gaps.
Every configured runtime family, with what it declares right now.
get.description:
A *freshly discovered* declaration, not a frozen one. That distinction is the
whole point of the route: a binding keeps answering with the capabilities it
was frozen at, and an operator asking "what can this runtime do today" is
asking a different question — one whose answer must never be written back onto
a binding.

get.summary: The sessions one runtime family currently owns.
get.description:
A read of the runtime, not of this Realm's log — so it is the one place an
operator can see a session that exists natively and has no binding here.

Adoption itself is deliberately absent: binding a native session to an agent run
creates a run, a binding and a frozen capability snapshot in one transaction, and
`CommandKind` has no variant that records that intent. Adding one is a
`kontor-core` change with its own compatibility matrix entry, which is a ticket
and not a route. Until then a discovered session is reported and nothing here
claims it.

404.description: This daemon is not configured with that runtime

get.summary: The Realm's current scheduling contention.

post.summary: Deliver one message into a session.
post.description:
The `Idempotency-Key` *is* the stable client message id: it must parse as one,
and it is what the runtime's own ledger keys the effect on. Requiring two
separate tokens would create two things that can disagree about whether a
retry is the same message, and only one of them would be the one the runtime
actually checks.

200.description: Delivered, or the original ack replayed

409.description: The id already committed different content

post.summary: Answer one permission request raised inside a session.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The runtime's own permission request id

200.description: Applied, or the original ack replayed

409.description: The request was already answered differently

422.description: This runtime cannot take permission answers

get.summary: Follow a session's content strictly after a validated timeline anchor.
get.description:
The anchor is required, and that is the transport spelling of "history anchors
live": without a position a previous read validated, there is nothing for
delivery to be strictly after, and a stream that guessed would be unable to
tell a runtime dropping events from its own missing start.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The anchor a timeline read returned

200.description: An SSE stream of session content

get.summary: One page of a session's recorded content, read from the runtime.
get.description:
The page is validated through `HistoryReader` before it is returned, so what a
caller receives is exactly-once by construction: a redelivered item is dropped
from the page rather than merely uncounted, and a page that changes epoch,
skips a sequence or rewrites a position it already delivered is refused.

409.description: The timeline must be refetched from the start

AccountDto.description:
One coding-account profile, as a policy reader sees it.

Three of the stored fields — the environment map, the routing metadata and the
declared capability document — are deliberately absent. Every one of them is
non-secret by construction, and every one of them is also the natural place a
deployment would eventually write an endpoint. A view that never carries them
cannot start carrying one by accident.

AppliedRevisionsDto.description:
Which pinned specification revisions an aggregate is running under.

Every one of these is a *frozen* revision copied into the aggregate, not a
pointer to whatever the current definition happens to be. That is what makes
a snapshot re-checkable rather than merely re-readable.

team_template.description: The team template the run's team pinned.

work_profile.description: The work profile the task's active workflow pinned.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family. Never an endpoint.

ContentionDto.description:
What is currently held, and therefore what a scheduling pass would contend
with.

This is evidence and **not a plan**. A plan is `kontor_scheduler::plan`'s
answer over a `SchedulingSnapshot`, and that snapshot needs authorization,
calendar, fleet-preflight and external-work evidence this build has no read
path for. Serving contention under an honest name is the difference between
telling an operator what is known and inventing a decision.

module_claims.description: Every live module claim in the Realm.

tasks_with_open_runs.description: Every task with an open run.

DecisionDto.description: What the pass decided about one candidate.

admitted.description: Whether the pass would admit it.

authorization_id.description: The authorization the pass would admit it under.

blockers.description:
Every blocker that refuses it, in evaluation order.

The first entry is always the code above: `explain` asks the same blockers
in the same order the decision does. Later entries are what an operator
would hit next after fixing the first, which is why they are here.

code.description: The one code the decision reports, for a refusal.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family it would launch through.

generation.description: The runtime generation it belongs to.

native_event_id.description: The runtime's own event id, when it provides one.

payload.description:

realm_id.description: The Realm it was recorded in.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family that reported it.

ProfileDto.description:
One resolved work-profile revision, as its phase and gate structure.

The whole [`kontor_core::spec::WorkProfileSpec`] is deliberately not served:
it carries a runtime-routing reference, and a read route is not the place to
start naming where runs go. What a caller needs to reason about a task is the
phase DAG and the gates, which is what this is.

ReceiptInspectionDto.description:
One command receipt and every state it has been through.

This is what makes an idempotent replay checkable rather than merely claimed:
a caller that retried a command can read the receipt its key recorded and see
that the history did not grow.

The stored correlation and native identity are deliberately absent, exactly as
they are from `ReceiptDto`: a correlation is the dispatcher's private handle on
a foreign system.

attempts.description: How many dispatch attempts have been made.

history.description: Every state it has been through, oldest first.

target_revision.description: The revision the intent was computed against.

replayed.description:
`true` when the idempotency key had already recorded this exact command,
so nothing was written and the original receipt is being returned.

ReceiptResponse.description: A receipt, and whether this call is the one that recorded it.

ReceiptTransitionDto.description: One step of a receipt's durable history.

sequence.description: Position in the receipt's history, starting at 1.

state.description: The state the receipt moved to.

TicketProjectionDto.description:
The projection this Realm computed for one ticket.

Published as `TicketProjectionDto` rather than under its Rust name. `utoipa`
keys the contract document by bare type name, and [`crate::dto::ProjectionDto`]
— the orthogonal state of a *run* — already holds `ProjectionDto` there. Two
registrations under one name do not collide loudly: the second silently
replaces the first, so `RunDto.projection` would resolve to this shape and
every generated client would be wrong about it while the wire stayed right.

confirmed_at.description:

profile.description: The profile key. An open, deployment-defined key.

version.description: The immutable revision of that key.

ViewDto_ProjectDto.description:
A Realm-qualified view.

The Realm is named on every answer for the same reason it is named on a
snapshot: a value that leaves this process is read as `(realm_id, …)` or not
at all.

realm_id.description: The Realm this view came from.

value.description: Read one project's identity and revision.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

ViewDto_ReceiptInspectionDto.description:
A Realm-qualified view.

The Realm is named on every answer for the same reason it is named on a
snapshot: a value that leaves this process is read as `(realm_id, …)` or not
at all.

realm_id.description: The Realm this view came from.

value.description:
One command receipt and every state it has been through.

This is what makes an idempotent replay checkable rather than merely claimed:
a caller that retried a command can read the receipt its key recorded and see
that the history did not grow.

The stored correlation and native identity are deliberately absent, exactly as
they are from `ReceiptDto`: a correlation is the dispatcher's private handle on
a foreign system.

attempts.description: How many dispatch attempts have been made.

history.description: Every state it has been through, oldest first.

target_revision.description: The revision the intent was computed against.

ViewDto_TicketDto.description:
A Realm-qualified view.

The Realm is named on every answer for the same reason it is named on a
snapshot: a value that leaves this process is read as `(realm_id, …)` or not
at all.

realm_id.description: The Realm this view came from.

value.description: One ticket, with the evidence this Realm holds about it.

oneOf.description:
The newest observation, or `null` when the ticket has never been observed.

This is where the *live* assignee and status appear, as last seen. It is an
observation and never a claim about now.
The newest projection, or `null` when none has been computed.

unresolved_conflicts.description: How many of those are still unresolved.

ViewDto_Vec_AccountDto.description:
A Realm-qualified view.

The Realm is named on every answer for the same reason it is named on a
snapshot: a value that leaves this process is read as `(realm_id, …)` or not
at all.

realm_id.description: The Realm this view came from.

items.description:
One coding-account profile, as a policy reader sees it.

Three of the stored fields — the environment map, the routing metadata and the
declared capability document — are deliberately absent. Every one of them is
non-secret by construction, and every one of them is also the natural place a
deployment would eventually write an endpoint. A view that never carries them
cannot start carrying one by accident.

credential_alias.description:
The opaque approved alias. Never a credential, and never where one
resolves to.

credential_kind.description: Which approved family the credential alias belongs to.

external_account_id.description: The external account id it authenticates as, when it records one.

harness.description: The runtime family it authenticates against.

provider_identity.description: The non-secret provider identity hint, when the deployment records one.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

author_display.description: The author's display name, when the external system provided one.

body_hash.description: The digest of the body, which is half this revision's identity.

external_comment_id.description: The external system's own comment id.

external_updated_at.description: When it was last edited externally.

supersedes_hash.description: The revision this one replaces, for an edit.

items.description: One native session a runtime currently owns.

bound.description:
Whether this Realm already holds a binding for it.

The point of a discovery read: a session the Realm does not know about is an
adoption candidate, and one it does know about is not.

generation.description: The runtime generation it belongs to.

host.description: The host label the runtime reports for itself.

native_id.description: The runtime's own session id. Correlation evidence, never an identity.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family that owns it.

ViewDto_Vec_RuntimeDto.description:
A Realm-qualified view.

The Realm is named on every answer for the same reason it is named on a

realm_id.description: The Realm this view came from.

items.description: What one configured runtime family reports about itself right now.

account_env.description: Whether it can prove which coding account a run executes as.

max_concurrent_sessions.description: How many concurrent sessions it declares.

max_history_page.description: The largest history page it declares.

max_message_bytes.description: The largest message it declares it will take, in bytes.

reachable.description:
Whether the runtime answered the capability question at all.

This is the health signal, and it is a fact about the channel: a family
that could not be reached reports `false` here and no capabilities, rather
than the capabilities it had last time.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family. Never an endpoint.

supported.description: The operations it currently declares, when it answered.

trust_grade.description: How much of what it reports may be acted on, when it answered.

items.description:
One task, as a list entry.

It is deliberately smaller than `TaskDto`: a list is for finding the task you
want, and the gates, the pinned revisions and the workflow are one read away
on the snapshot route.

module.description: The module it contends for, if any.

acknowledged_at.description: When the external system acknowledged it.

assignment_prerequisite.description: Whether an assignment had to happen first.

confirmed_at.description:
When a *refetched* observation confirmed it.

`null` means unconfirmed, which is never the same as failed: an
acknowledgement is not a confirmation, and this column is only written when
the external system was read again.

milestone.description: The internal milestone being converged to.

principal_account_id.description: The external principal it acted as.

target_status_id.description: The external status it aimed at.

task_id.description: The task whose state was being projected.

transition_id.description: The external transition used. `null` for an assignee-only convergence.

realm_bearer.description: One of the realm's tier secrets, read from its 0600 credential file.
